/data/title	Conical Bowl with Interior of Fish Swimming amid Waves Encircling a Sea Crab and Exterior of Stylized Petals
/data/main_reference_number	2013.228
/data/date_display	Jin dynasty (1115–1234), 12th century
/data/place_of_origin	China
/data/description	Potters from Yaozhou used a carved mold to decorate the interior of this bowl, making the process of production more efficient. Remarkably, this accelerated approach to decoration did not compromise the beauty of the final product. Inside the bowl, four fishes gracefully encircle a sea creature — either a crab or a squid — amidst the rippling waves. The surface of the bowl is fully covered in a glossy, translucent olive-green glaze. The glaze pools in the recesses, producing a slightly deeper hue that enhances the dynamism and vividness of the motifs. When filled with water or tea, the bowl brings the marine animals to life by creating an illusion of them swimming within the liquid.
/data/dimensions	4.1 × 9.6 cm (1 5/8 × 3 13/16 in.); Diam.: 9.6 cm (3 13/16 in.)
/data/medium_display	Yaozhou ware; stoneware with underglaze molded and carved decoration
/data/credit_line	Gift of Dorothy Braude Edinburg to the Harry B. and Bessie K. Braude Memorial Collection
/data/provenance_text	Dorothy Braude Edinburg (1921-2015), Brookline, MA.; given to the Art Institute of Chicago, 2013.
